gates.text: The plan is the deliverable, not implementation.
For one or two files with an obvious approach, say a multi-phase plan is unnecessary and stop.
Otherwise preserve these gates.
Settle each observable open question with the [prototype](#prototype) workflow before writing the plan.
Keep task-owned branch and SHA evidence and screenshots or observed outputs for Appendix A.
The prototype is throwaway, not production implementation.
Only a genuine product or preference decision no run can settle goes to the operator with options.
Missing prototype authority or runtime is BLOCKED, not guessed evidence.
Explore the affected code with scoped native readers.
Resolve `how explorer` through `pstack_route` and use emitted native `sessions_spawn` arguments.
Each reader returns file pointers, conventions, test commands, and entry points, not source dumps.
Required exploration that cannot run is BLOCKED, never a silent sequential parent substitute.
Write to the operator's path or a task-owned docs directory.
Keep every heading and sub-block in the skeleton below, in order, fill every placeholder, and use one section per PR with its own evidence.

Name the execution route and merger in How to read this: [autopilot-full](#autopilot-full) when the run may merge, [autopilot-stack](#autopilot-stack) when the operator lands the PRs, or [orchestrate](#orchestrate) for a standing program.
The plan never grants publication authority.
Apply [technical-writing](workflows.md#technical-writing), then [unslop](workflows.md#unslop).
The body is a how-to; appendices hold explanation and references.
Use task headings, plain sentences, no long dashes or mid-sentence connector colons.
The short introduction is under ten nonblank lines.
Every verification block opens with the exact verification rule below.
Unit tests alone do not verify a PR.

Require ten independent live lanes at its exact head using `pstack_route` and emitted native `sessions_spawn` arguments for `swarm workers`, each with a concrete scenario, saved screenshot path, and pass predicate.
One is the Regression lane against trunk.
A missing trunk feature is recorded honestly; gate the added behavior and user-visible end state rather than invent a trunk result.
A missing capture or driver is a BLOCKED live gate, not removal of that block.
Pick native browser/computer, CLI, or simulator controls by actual surface; two surfaces need lanes on both.
Record missing control capability in Appendix C and still name the intended driver.
Perf verification names Metric, Probe, Baseline, and Rule.
Measure trunk first, then interleave trunk and head with both producing the named metric and a numeric failure threshold.
If scenarios differ because trunk lacks the feature, prohibit an invalid ratio and add absolute budgets for diff-added work and the user-visible end state.
A PR changing an interaction needs operator review in chat with screenshots and a 30 to 60 second video before merge.
A non-interaction PR says `**Review gate.** None. PR-1 is not review-gated.` using its real PR id and has no boxes there.

The program checklist must specify explicit-go arming, dependency order, one owner per PR, exact file boundaries, native PR mechanics, committed-head checks, comment review, code-ready and merge-ready receipts, verification and patch-id rules, boot commands, and stop propagation.
Full verification names one gates lane, ten live lanes, one perf lane, and at least two focused audit lanes.
Root audits receipts before a clean verdict.
New behavior, redesign, or large diffs rerun the full swarm; minor fixes and rebases need a new-head verifier unless patch-id evidence carries a lane.
Missing or failed mandatory gates still block.
Native automation is only a separately authorized bounded owner lifecycle, not an upstream loop command or a plan-created timer.
Resolve `scripts/plan-check.mjs` from the installed pstack skill directory and run `node /absolute/path/to/pstack/scripts/plan-check.mjs /absolute/path/to/plan.md`; fix every diagnostic.
Source-checkout behavioral tests run with `node --test tests/plan-check.test.mjs`.
It is a read-only structural gate, not proof that the plan's experiments, permissions, or evidence are valid.
If the shipped helper is unavailable, report the checker gate BLOCKED, never run the pinned upstream script.
Hand back the path, PR ids and dependencies, review-gated set, prototype conclusions and unknowns, and the actual checker output, then stop.
Execution begins only on the operator's explicit go under the named execution playbook.
Keep this skeleton, replacing angle-bracket placeholders with concrete evidence-producing tasks.
The example is deliberately incomplete until filled.
# <Program> plan
<Who benefits, what changes, the governing rule, and ordered PR ids. Under ten lines.>
## How to read this
One box is one unit of work. Every box names the evidence that checks it.
Check a box only when its evidence exists, such as a file, log, screenshot, run, or SHA.
The body is a how-to. Appendices explain and record.
The program runs playbooks/<execution route>. <Who merges and which items stop at merge-ready.>
Tests alone are not sufficient verification. A PR is verified only when its unit, live, and perf boxes are all checked.
## Program checklist
### Arm the program
- [ ] State the protocol and plan, then stop until the operator's explicit go.
- [ ] Read the execution playbook, swarm, installed control skill, opening-a-pr, and other used native leaves from the approved trunk revision at start and each audit.
- [ ] Record the authorized native audit lifecycle or its BLOCKED gate, owner, cadence, deadline, and budget. No timer is created by this plan.

- [ ] Audit prompt. Re-read the execution route, inspect every active lane's side effects, record heads and runs, replace stuck work only after custody is safe, repair drift, and append a trail row. Send a status message only for unreported tracked changes or a new operator decision. No repeated unchanged status.
- [ ] Propagate the operator's hold as zero-writes to every owner and leaf.
### Spawn owners
- [ ] Use `pstack_route` and emitted native `sessions_spawn` arguments for one owner per PR with the full lifecycle named by the execution playbook.
- [ ] <Concrete dependency graph and branching order.>
- [ ] <Exclusive file boundaries per PR.>
- [ ] <Interaction-changing PR ids requiring screenshots and video review.>
### PR mechanics, for every PR
- [ ] <Authorized native forge and PR creation operation, ready or explicitly required draft, correct base.>
- [ ] <Repo lint, typecheck, focused tests on committed head before push. Hooks stay enabled.>
- [ ] <Scope cleanup before commit, no-comments before review, and concrete review-thread triage.>

- [ ] <Owner code-ready rebase onto trunk or the real dependency parent, later head receipts, self-proof and babysit. Fix rounds rebase for conflict, trunk-caused CI or known concurrent same-file landing; merge prep retains its own rule.>
### Verdict and merge, for every PR
- [ ] <Code-ready full swarm with one gates lane, ten live lanes, perf lane, and at least two audit lanes. Minor-fix new-head verifier rule and wording-only exception preserving mandatory gates.>
- [ ] <Root receipt audit, demonstrated blocking findings and mandatory gates clear, trunk regressions recorded separately, scoped owner fix-forward and patch-id requalification.>
- [ ] <Authorized owner merge rule, or verified no-merge handoff and operator landing; stack only real dependencies.>
### Boot recipe, for every live lane
- [ ] <Isolated authorized environment, exact head checkout, backend and surface start, ready predicate.>
- [ ] <Named native control driver for input and read-only diagnostics.>
- [ ] <Per-lane screenshot and report paths.>
